trace.title: Filipina tennis star Alex Eala is spotted seated in the front row beside Vogue’s Anna Wint

data.text:
Filipina tennis star Alex Eala is spotted seated in the front row beside Vogue’s Anna Wintour at the Michael Kors fashion show during New York Fashion Week.
“We had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion. How she wants to learn about it and follow it and I think it’s great,” Anna previously said in an interview at the US Open.

output.title: Alex Eala gets spotlight from this brand at New York Fashion Week
output.description: It’s Alex Eala’s time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court.
output.text: It's Alex Eala 's time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court. On Instagram, the Filipina tennis ace got her own spotlight on the Calvin Klein account during the New York Fashion Week. Alex attended the brand's Spring 2027 runway show wearing a relaxed white long-sleeved button-down shirt paired with off-white slacks and pointed-toe heels. Following her third-round finish at this year's US Open, Alex made her New York Fashion Week debut when she attended the Tory Burch show. Earlier, Kelsey Merritt shared a photo with Alex after the two met at the Michael Kors show. Beyond tennis, Alex has also expressed her interest in fashion . During her latest visit to Manila in July, she said incorporating Filipino elements into her outfits while on tour is her way of paying tribute to her roots. Alex added that she is interested in collaborating with Filipino designers for future engagements. Meanwhile, Alex is set to headline the event " Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate " on December 8 at the Philippine Arena. She will face fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in the exhibition match. output.description: Alex Eala joined Vogue’s Anna Wintour in the front row at the Michael Kors fashion show.

text.preview: Filipina tennis star Alex Eala was spotted seated in the front row beside Vogue’s Anna Wintour at the Michael Kors fashion show during New York Fashion Week. Television host Keltie Knight shared a clip on TikTok showing Alex sitting next to the renowned fashion editor at the event. “ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour,” Keltie wrote. Fans online were quick to react to the moment. “Wow! Alex with Anna Wintour.. 😳😳😳 Tennis star to fashionista ❤️,” one fan wrote. @keltieknight ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour ♬ Danceteria - Madonna Anna previously shared how Alex caught her attention, particularly because of the young athlete’s growing interest in fashion and willingness to learn more about the industry. “We had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion. How she wants to learn about it and follow it and I think it’s great,” she said in an interview at the US Open. “It’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage,” she added. Aside from the Michael Kors show, Alex also attended the fashion shows of Tory Burch and Calvin Klein during the New York Fashion Week. Tory Burch marked Alex's first event at NYFW. In an interview with Cultured Magazine, Alex reflected on the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. "Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she highlighted. At the Calvin Klein show, Alex also landed a front-row seat alongside several international stars, including Sadie Sink, Tate McRae, and Lingling Kwong. output.title: Next fashion icon? Alex Eala gets attention of former Vogue editor Anna Wintour | ABS-CBN Lifestyle
output.description: The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala.
output.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. output.title: Anna Wintour takes notice of Alex Eala
output.description: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion.

text.preview: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala ’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion. In a video shared by the US Open on social media, Anna discussed how athletes such as Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka have used fashion as a way to express themselves. “Well, I think it’s really interesting, especially when you look at players obviously like Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it,” the fashion icon said. She then pointed to Alex as another young player who is showing an interest in the fashion world. “And we had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Anna said. “And I think it’s great, it’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage.” Anna gave the quick interview at sidelines of the US Open exhibition match of Roger Federer and Andy Roddick , where Alex was present with fellow tennis player Eva Lys. On Instagram Stories, Eva posted a photo with the Filipina star and wrote, "We're spectators today." Alex shared Eva's post. Vogue Magazine meanwhile shared a reel from the event that showed Anna engaging with Serena Williams and Gayle King, and Alex and Eva welcoming Vogue to the US Open. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vogue (@voguemagazine) Alex wore a cropped mustard leather top and paired it with jeans to the event. Even through fashion and accessories, Alex has proudly been representing the Philippines . Earlier this week, she donned our humble ol' tsineles that made her outfit look casually chic. Before that Alex wore pink sampaguita earrings at the Canadian Open. She also donned a sampaguita-themed hair tie in Wimbledon 2025 and a custom visor in 2026 , which had the Filipino phrase "Kapag lumago, hindi na hihinto." Alex will be competing in the US Open. output.description: By ELIZABETH LOLARGA “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. text.preview: “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. Filipino Style , a 1997 de luxe book put out by the Department of Tourism in time for the country’s national centennial in ’98 and preceding the current soft-cover Philippine Style: Design and Architecture (Anvil Publishing Inc.), used that word long before it became the vogue adjective for food that takes in a variety of cultural influences. “Three hundred years in the convent, 50 in Hollywood and a brief interlude with the Japanese”–that was how eminent writer Carmen Guerrero Nakpil described the country’s colonial history and its three former masters (Spain, the US and Japan). The last didn’t quite seep in, except maybe in the sleek lines of modern architecture. Today, hard-earned dollars from overseas Filipino workers have made possible the rise of a hodge-podge of architecture flecking the countryside with houses derivative of Mediterranean villas or Mexican landlords’ haciendas and assorted misadvised kitsch coming from new money. There seems to be no acknowledgment of the wisdom inherent in the humble bahay kubo (native hut) or the gentry’s bahay na bato (house of stone), especially their factoring in of climate (harsh sun, torrential rains) and site. Architect Dominic Galicia points out in the introduction to Philippine Style that the kubo has a “geometric simplicity: a pyramidal roof hovering like a parasol over a bamboo box of stilts. Rain slid off the steeply pitched cogon roof, while fresh air, flowing in through the slatted floor and the wide windows, cooled the interior before exiting through the permeable roof thatch.” Even the Spanish-influenced bahay na bato considered the kubo an elegant and “simple solution to climate control.” Today’s discerning architect refers to these structures from the past to build buildings and houses. output.title: 50 Years: A fiesta of Philippine design
output.description: Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024.

text.preview: Images courtesy of R.C. Ladrido and BluPrint Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue. Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s. A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.” Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines. Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance. She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022. Arturo Luz (1926-2021): A painter, printmaker, sculptor, and designer known for his abstract paintings and wood and metal sculptures, he was a founding director of the Metropolitan Museum of Manila in 1976 to 1986 and also appointed as the head of the Design Center of the Philippines. output.title: Alex Eala meets Anna Wintour, Sadie Sink at New York Fashion Week
output.description: The Filipina tennis ace hobnobbed with several Hollywood stars and a fashion icon.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala had a star-studded encounter off the court as she crossed paths with fashion icon Anna Wintour and Hollywood actresses Sadie Sink and Amanda Seyfried during New York Fashion Week. Eala attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 show in New York, where she was seated in the front row alongside Wintour and was in the same room with Amanda Seyfriend and musician Lauryn Hill. She also attended the Calvin Klein show with actresses Pamela Anderson, Sadie Sink, Tate McRae and Gemma Chan. The appearance marked Eala’s debut at New York Fashion Week, adding another milestone to what has been a remarkable year for the 20-year-old athlete. Eala has previously caught Wintour’s attention for her growing interest in fashion. During an interview in August, Wintour cited Eala while discussing how tennis players have increasingly used fashion to express their personalities. Wintour mentioned tennis icons Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka before turning her attention to Eala, whom she described as a young Filipino star who is already showing an interest in fashion. “You could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Wintour said. Eala admitted to Culture maganzine that she was both excited and nervous attending her first fashion week. “I’m so excited. I’m a little nervous. There’s some amazing people in this room. I’m so happy to be a part of it,” she said. She also noted the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. “Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality,” she said. The tennis star attended the Tory Burch presentation in a red blazer paired with a blue-gray striped shirt and wide brown trousers. output.title: Alex Eala goes black, white for Michael Kors, Calvin Klein New York shows
output.description: Alex Eala is continuing to take the fashion world by storm.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala is continuing to take the fashion world by storm by attending more New York Fashion Week shows. Fresh from her 3rd round exit in the US Open, Alex made her fashion week debut by attending the Spring/Summer 2027 collection launch of Tory Burch last September 10, Thursday. The tennister was invited as an athlete guest seated front row, opting for a red blazer with black buttons, a blue-gray striped shirt underneath, and wide brown slacks. "I'm so excited. I'm a little nervous. There's some amazing people in this room. I'm so happy to be a part of it. You know, my mom growing up really had a lot of Tory Burch shoes," Alex said at the sidelines of the red carpet. "Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she continued. "Sports is very physically demanding and fashion, maybe come back to me after this week and I'll know more about it." Related: Alex Eala makes fashion week debut in New York for Tory Burch The following day Alex showed up at the Museum of Modern Art's Sculpture Garden for the Spring/Summer 2027 collection of Michael Kors, this time donning a little black dress, matching gloves, and kitten heels. Among the attendees for that show were Lea Michele, Gabrielle Union, Olivia Munn, Kathryn Newton, Aaron Tveit, Lori Harvey, Chloe Fineman, and Natalia Bryant. The athlete also sat front row for Calvin Klein's Spring 2027 collection by Veronica Leoni, seated in a white ensemble alongside Sadie Sink, Pamela Anderson, Gemma Chan, and Tate McRae. Speaking to a fashion magazine, the young tennis star praised Calvin Klein's recent campaigns with Sadie and Rosalia. "I love that in tennis we're able to express ourselves through fashion. I know that in a lot of sports maybe it's a little more restrictive," Alex said. "You're able to show your personality in both worlds, and you know, I'm excited to explore more." articles.title: Defining Philippine style
articles.description: By ELIZABETH LOLARGA “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. text.preview: “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. Filipino Style , a 1997 de luxe book put out by the Department of Tourism in time for the country’s national centennial in ’98 and preceding the current soft-cover Philippine Style: Design and Architecture (Anvil Publishing Inc.), used that word long before it became the vogue adjective for food that takes in a variety of cultural influences. “Three hundred years in the convent, 50 in Hollywood and a brief interlude with the Japanese”–that was how eminent writer Carmen Guerrero Nakpil described the country’s colonial history and its three former masters (Spain, the US and Japan). The last didn’t quite seep in, except maybe in the sleek lines of modern architecture. Today, hard-earned dollars from overseas Filipino workers have made possible the rise of a hodge-podge of architecture flecking the countryside with houses derivative of Mediterranean villas or Mexican landlords’ haciendas and assorted misadvised kitsch coming from new money. There seems to be no acknowledgment of the wisdom inherent in the humble bahay kubo (native hut) or the gentry’s bahay na bato (house of stone), especially their factoring in of climate (harsh sun, torrential rains) and site. Architect Dominic Galicia points out in the introduction to Philippine Style that the kubo has a “geometric simplicity: a pyramidal roof hovering like a parasol over a bamboo box of stilts. Rain slid off the steeply pitched cogon roof, while fresh air, flowing in through the slatted floor and the wide windows, cooled the interior before exiting through the permeable roof thatch.” Even the Spanish-influenced bahay na bato considered the kubo an elegant and “simple solution to climate control.” Today’s discerning architect refers to these structures from the past to build buildings and houses. articles.title: 50 Years: A fiesta of Philippine design
articles.description: Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024.

text.preview: Images courtesy of R.C. Ladrido and BluPrint Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue. Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s. A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.” Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines. Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance. She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022. Arturo Luz (1926-2021): A painter, printmaker, sculptor, and designer known for his abstract paintings and wood and metal sculptures, he was a founding director of the Metropolitan Museum of Manila in 1976 to 1986 and also appointed as the head of the Design Center of the Philippines. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.” Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines. Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance. She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022. articles.title: Next fashion icon? Alex Eala gets attention of former Vogue editor Anna Wintour | ABS-CBN Lifestyle
articles.description: The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala.
articles.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. articles.title: Anna Wintour takes notice of Alex Eala

articles.title: Next fashion icon? Alex Eala gets attention of former Vogue editor Anna Wintour | ABS-CBN Lifestyle
articles.description: The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala.
articles.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. Alex Eala proudly wears Filipiniana at Laureus Awards in Madrid

articles.text: It's Alex Eala 's time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court. On Instagram, the Filipina tennis ace got her own spotlight on the Calvin Klein account during the New York Fashion Week. Alex attended the brand's Spring 2027 runway show wearing a relaxed white long-sleeved button-down shirt paired with off-white slacks and pointed-toe heels. During her latest visit to Manila in July, she said incorporating Filipino elements into her outfits while on tour is her way of paying tribute to her roots. Alex added that she is interested in collaborating with Filipino designers for future engagements. Meanwhile, Alex is set to headline the event " Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate " on December 8 at the Philippine Arena. She will face fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in the exhibition match. articles.title: Anna Wintour takes notice of Alex Eala
articles.description: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion.

text.preview: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala ’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion. In a video shared by the US Open on social media, Anna discussed how athletes such as Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka have used fashion as a way to express themselves. “Well, I think it’s really interesting, especially when you look at players obviously like Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it,” the fashion icon said. She then pointed to Alex as another young player who is showing an interest in the fashion world. “And we had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Anna said. “And I think it’s great, it’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage.” Anna gave the quick interview at sidelines of the US Open exhibition match of Roger Federer and Andy Roddick , where Alex was present with fellow tennis player Eva Lys. On Instagram Stories, Eva posted a photo with the Filipina star and wrote, "We're spectators today." Alex shared Eva's post. Vogue Magazine meanwhile shared a reel from the event that showed Anna engaging with Serena Williams and Gayle King, and Alex and Eva welcoming Vogue to the US Open. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vogue (@voguemagazine) Alex wore a cropped mustard leather top and paired it with jeans to the event. Even through fashion and accessories, Alex has proudly been representing the Philippines . Earlier this week, she donned our humble ol' tsineles that made her outfit look casually chic. Before that Alex wore pink sampaguita earrings at the Canadian Open. She also donned a sampaguita-themed hair tie in Wimbledon 2025 and a custom visor in 2026 , which had the Filipino phrase "Kapag lumago, hindi na hihinto." Alex will be competing in the US Open. articles.description: The Filipina tennis ace hobnobbed with several Hollywood stars and a fashion icon.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala had a star-studded encounter off the court as she crossed paths with fashion icon Anna Wintour and Hollywood actresses Sadie Sink and Amanda Seyfried during New York Fashion Week. Eala attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 show in New York, where she was seated in the front row alongside Wintour and was in the same room with Amanda Seyfriend and musician Lauryn Hill. She also attended the Calvin Klein show with actresses Pamela Anderson, Sadie Sink, Tate McRae and Gemma Chan. The appearance marked Eala’s debut at New York Fashion Week, adding another milestone to what has been a remarkable year for the 20-year-old athlete. Eala has previously caught Wintour’s attention for her growing interest in fashion. During an interview in August, Wintour cited Eala while discussing how tennis players have increasingly used fashion to express their personalities. Wintour mentioned tennis icons Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka before turning her attention to Eala, whom she described as a young Filipino star who is already showing an interest in fashion. “You could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Wintour said. Eala admitted to Culture maganzine that she was both excited and nervous attending her first fashion week. “I’m so excited. I’m a little nervous. There’s some amazing people in this room. I’m so happy to be a part of it,” she said. She also noted the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. “Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality,” she said. The tennis star attended the Tory Burch presentation in a red blazer paired with a blue-gray striped shirt and wide brown trousers. Her New York Fashion Week appearance came after her recent campaign at the US Open, where she advanced to the third round. A post shared by Alexandra Ea

article.title: 50 Years: A fiesta of Philippine design
article.description: Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024.

text.preview: Images courtesy of R.C. Ladrido and BluPrint Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue. Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s. A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.” Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines. Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance. She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022. Arturo Luz (1926-2021): A painter, printmaker, sculptor, and designer known for his abstract paintings and wood and metal sculptures, he was a founding director of the Metropolitan Museum of Manila in 1976 to 1986 and also appointed as the head of the Design Center of the Philippines. article.description: The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala.
article.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. articles.title: Next fashion icon? Alex Eala gets attention of former Vogue editor Anna Wintour | ABS-CBN Lifestyle
articles.description: The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala.
articles.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. Alex Eala proudly wears Filipiniana at Laureus Awards in Madrid

articles.title: Alex Eala gets spotlight from this brand at New York Fashion Week
articles.description: It’s Alex Eala’s time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court.
articles.text: It's Alex Eala 's time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court. On Instagram, the Filipina tennis ace got her own spotlight on the Calvin Klein account during the New York Fashion Week. Alex attended the brand's Spring 2027 runway show wearing a relaxed white long-sleeved button-down shirt paired with off-white slacks and pointed-toe heels. Following her third-round finish at this year's US Open, Alex made her New York Fashion Week debut when she attended the Tory Burch show. Earlier, Kelsey Merritt shared a photo with Alex after the two met at the Michael Kors show. Beyond tennis, Alex has also expressed her interest in fashion . During her latest visit to Manila in July, she said incorporating Filipino elements into her outfits while on tour is her way of paying tribute to her roots. Alex added that she is interested in collaborating with Filipino designers for future engagements. Meanwhile, Alex is set to headline the event " Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate " on December 8 at the Philippine Arena. She will face fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in the exhibition match. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Calvin Klein (@calvinklein) —Hermes Joy Tunac/MGP GMA News

articles.title: Anna Wintour takes notice of Alex Eala
articles.description: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion.

text.preview: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala ’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion. In a video shared by the US Open on social media, Anna discussed how athletes such as Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka have used fashion as a way to express themselves. “Well, I think it’s really interesting, especially when you look at players obviously like Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it,” the fashion icon said. She then pointed to Alex as another young player who is showing an interest in the fashion world. “And we had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Anna said. “And I think it’s great, it’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage.” Anna gave the quick interview at sidelines of the US Open exhibition match of Roger Federer and Andy Roddick , where Alex was present with fellow tennis player Eva Lys. On Instagram Stories, Eva posted a photo with the Filipina star and wrote, "We're spectators today." Alex shared Eva's post. Vogue Magazine meanwhile shared a reel from the event that showed Anna engaging with Serena Williams and Gayle King, and Alex and Eva welcoming Vogue to the US Open. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vogue (@voguemagazine) Alex wore a cropped mustard leather top and paired it with jeans to the event. Even through fashion and accessories, Alex has proudly been representing the Philippines . Earlier this week, she donned our humble ol' tsineles that made her outfit look casually chic. Before that Alex wore pink sampaguita earrings at the Canadian Open. She also donned a sampaguita-themed hair tie in Wimbledon 2025 and a custom visor in 2026 , which had the Filipino phrase "Kapag lumago, hindi na hihinto." Alex will be competing in the US Open. articles.title: Alex Eala meets Anna Wintour, Sadie Sink at New York Fashion Week
articles.description: The Filipina tennis ace hobnobbed with several Hollywood stars and a fashion icon.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala had a star-studded encounter off the court as she crossed paths with fashion icon Anna Wintour and Hollywood actresses Sadie Sink and Amanda Seyfried during New York Fashion Week. Eala attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 show in New York, where she was seated in the front row alongside Wintour and was in the same room with Amanda Seyfriend and musician Lauryn Hill. She also attended the Calvin Klein show with actresses Pamela Anderson, Sadie Sink, Tate McRae and Gemma Chan. The appearance marked Eala’s debut at New York Fashion Week, adding another milestone to what has been a remarkable year for the 20-year-old athlete. Eala has previously caught Wintour’s attention for her growing interest in fashion. During an interview in August, Wintour cited Eala while discussing how tennis players have increasingly used fashion to express their personalities. Wintour mentioned tennis icons Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka before turning her attention to Eala, whom she described as a young Filipino star who is already showing an interest in fashion. “You could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Wintour said. Eala admitted to Culture maganzine that she was both excited and nervous attending her first fashion week. “I’m so excited. I’m a little nervous. There’s some amazing people in this room. I’m so happy to be a part of it,” she said. She also noted the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. “Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality,” she said. The tennis star attended the Tory Burch presentation in a red blazer paired with a blue-gray striped shirt and wide brown trousers. Her New York Fashion Week appearance came after her recent campaign at the US Open, where she advanced to the third round. A post shared by Alexandra Ea

articles.title: Alex Eala goes black, white for Michael Kors, Calvin Klein New York shows
articles.description: Alex Eala is continuing to take the fashion world by storm.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala is continuing to take the fashion world by storm by attending more New York Fashion Week shows. Fresh from her 3rd round exit in the US Open, Alex made her fashion week debut by attending the Spring/Summer 2027 collection launch of Tory Burch last September 10, Thursday. The tennister was invited as an athlete guest seated front row, opting for a red blazer with black buttons, a blue-gray striped shirt underneath, and wide brown slacks. "I'm so excited. I'm a little nervous. There's some amazing people in this room. I'm so happy to be a part of it. You know, my mom growing up really had a lot of Tory Burch shoes," Alex said at the sidelines of the red carpet. "Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she continued. "Sports is very physically demanding and fashion, maybe come back to me after this week and I'll know more about it." passages.text: “FUSION”
seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors.

Filipino Style , a 1997 de luxe book put out by the Department of Tourism in time for the country’s national centennial in ’98 and preceding the current soft-cover Philippine Style: Design and Architecture (Anvil Publishing Inc.), used that word long before it became the vogue adjective for food that takes in a variety of cultural influences.

“Three hundred years in the convent, 50 in Hollywood and a brief interlude with the Japanese”–that was how eminent writer Carmen Guerrero Nakpil described the country’s colonial history and its three former masters (Spain, the US and Japan).
The last didn’t quite seep in, except maybe in the sleek lines of modern architecture.

Today, hard-earned dollars from overseas Filipino workers have made possible the rise of a hodge-podge of architecture flecking the countryside with houses derivative of Mediterranean villas or Mexican landlords’ haciendas and assorted misadvised kitsch coming from new money.

There seems to be no acknowledgment of the wisdom inherent in the humble bahay kubo (native hut) or the gentry’s bahay na bato (house of stone), especially their factoring in of climate (harsh sun, torrential rains) and site.

Architect Dominic Galicia points out in the introduction to Philippine Style that the kubo has a “geometric simplicity: a pyramidal roof hovering like a parasol over a bamboo box of stilts. Rain slid off the steeply pitched cogon roof, while fresh air, flowing in through the slatted floor and the wide windows, cooled the interior before exiting through the permeable roof thatch.”
Even the Spanish-influenced bahay na bato considered the kubo an elegant and “simple solution to climate control.”
Today’s discerning architect refers to these structures from the past to build buildings and houses.

The book is full of examples of how parts of old houses that are increasingly being demolished to make way for townhouses and multi-purpose condominiums (combining malls with floors of living and office spaces) can still be saved, reclaimed and recycled.
Besides, “retro” and “shabby chic” are quite in with new home owners who are enlightened enough by the high-profile environmental cause to nod respectfully towards Nature in building their houses.
Philippine Style , with contributed articles by Galicia, Ateneo Prof. Rene Javellana, Elizabeth V. Reyes, Joan Pasagui and Luca Tettoni, is both a scholarly and handy guide.
It acknowledges the works of great Filipino architects (Juan Arellano, Andres Luna de San Pedro, Fernando Ocampo, Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, Leandro Locsin, Gabriel Formoso, the brothers Mañosa).

It gives generous visual space to the inroads made by such innovative designers and aesthetes like Kenneth Cobonpue, Budji Layug, Milo Naval, Ino Manalo, Tina Periquet, Anna Sy, Benji Reyes who have drawn from Filipino materials and idioms in design in their works or cultural projects.

Cobonpue is a fine example of one who blends modern sensibility with Filipino fibers (rattan, buri , abaca , bamboo), helping him attain his stature as a “celebrity designer” for the likes of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie.
Architect Rosario “Ning” Encarnacion Tan has almost waged a heroic one-woman battle in behalf of “bamboo’s possibilities.”

She is quoted as saying, “Bamboo was seen as a poor man’s material, not strong and sturdy. Actually, bamboo is the ideal generic medium to express what is vernacular, authentic, sustainable, culture, reflective, and spiritual.”

Her bamboo houses are unique for they are “portable and dismantleable,” i.e., they can be assembled in one space and moved to another, just like the bahay kubo of old portrayed in paintings as a form of bayanihan , with the town’s menfolk carrying the hut on poles on their shoulders.

At a time when the progressive green movement is calling for a moratorium on large-scale logging to maintain the country’s forest cover, the book includes towards the end a “Glossary of Natural Materials.”

The lay reader can get acquainted with the many uses, including medicinal ones, of precious Philippine hardwoods ( tindalo , lanite , dao ) and learn to appreciate the beauty as well as usefulness of the capiz , cogon grass, piña , nipa, rattan, adobe.
Philippine Style also has a section devoted to designers’ portfolios that again show how a contemporary look can be achieved with traditional materials.
A Yoda easy chair is made of natural rattan vines woven onto a steel frame.
A Lulu easy chair has strands of abaca rope wrapped over a light steel frame.
As for accessorizing the home, the book is big on patronizing our very own, the stoneware makers among them.

Highlighted are the “whimsical stoneware” of Jon and Tessy Pettyjohn, Lanelle Abueva Fernando, Ugu Bigyan, the last earning a reputation for shaping pottery from forms drawn from nature and manmade creations like crochet lace.
Their works have, in a manner of speaking, fired up the ceramic industry.

Images courtesy of R.C. Ladrido and BluPrint Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024.

Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship.
Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue.

Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s.
A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.”
Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines.

Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance.
She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020.
She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022.

Arturo Luz (1926-2021): A painter, printmaker, sculptor, and designer known for his abstract paintings and wood and metal sculptures, he was a founding director of the Metropolitan Museum of Manila in 1976 to 1986 and also appointed as the head of the Design Center of the Philippines.
In 1997, he was conferred National Artist for Visual Arts.

Francisco “Bobby” Mañosa (1931-2019): A renowned champion of Filipino architecture in his 60 years of architectural practice, he created “original Filipino forms, spaces with intricate and refined details” in his myriad reinterpretation of the bahay kubo and bahay na bato .
He was conferred National Artist for Architecture and Allied Arts in 2018.
Among his major works: Sulo Hotel, Quezon City;
San Miguel Building, Ortigas Center, Pasig City;
Metrorail Transport System Stations for LRT 1;
Our Lady of Peace Shrine, EDSA, Quezon City;
Tahanang Pilipino (Coconut Palace), CCP Complex, Pasay;
and Amanpulo Resort, Palawan.
Narda Capuyan (d.2016): A family planning nurse, she introduced hand-knitting to women in Bontoc, Mountain Province to discourage them from making more babies.
Using recycled yarns, Narda and her team started weaving blankets and bedcovers in ikat design.
It was Narda’s mother who taught her the traditional art of hand-tying and dyeing threads, and weaving them into patterns called ikat.
One of her first breaks came in 1974 when Hyatt Terraces Baguio used her fabrics as hotel upholstery, curtains, bedcovers, and furnishings.
In 1982, Bloomingale Department Store in New York featured Narda’s products in a Philippine exhibition.
It all sold out.
Revitalizing the Cordillera weaving tradition, she received the 1982 Golden Shell Award for excellence in exports and for reviving ikat.
In 1989, she received the Countryside Investor Award, and the Agora Awards from the Philippine Marketing Association for her outstanding achievement in export marketing.
Raymundo Albano (1947-1985): A writer, curator, artist, he was a museum director of the Cultural Center of the Philippines where he worked from 1970 to 1981.
In CCP, he institutionalized “its program of abstraction, experimental performances, installations, new media of young Filipino artists.”
He also designed and produced CCP’s exhibition catalogues, posters, and magazines.
Kenneth Cobonpue (b.
1968): a multi-awarded industrial designer and manufacturer from Cebu, he has a degree in industrial design (1991) from the Pratt Institute New York.
In 1998, he started his own business known for artistic and handmade design that integrated traditional crafts and technology.
He established the industrial design program of the University of the Philippines Cebu in 2005.
Among his numerous awards: the first Maison et Objet Designer of the Year in Asia, 2014;
Gawad sa Sining Award, Cultural Center of the Philippines, 2020;
and Pratt Legends Award of 2023, Pratt Institute New York.

A leitmotif in the exhibition is the use of indigenous and sustainable materials, mostly plants (bamboo, buri, abaca, rattan, coconut, capiz, nito, piña, cotton)—all pressing concerns amidst environmental destruction and extreme climate change that have affected numerous countries today, including the Philippines.
Marian Pastor Roces has noted that it takes a village to bring forth Philippine design.
Behind every designer is a community, a collective effort that deals with sourcing raw materials, providing labor, and drawing from a deep well of craftmanship to create that single object of design.

In the end, it is the artistic DNA running through traditional artisans from Abra to Zamboanga — the nameless weavers, embroiderers, sewers, gold- and silversmiths, potters, woodcarvers, metalworkers, carpenters — who remain the life and energy of Philippine design.

text.preview: “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. Filipino Style , a 1997 de luxe book put out by the Department of Tourism in time for the country’s national centennial in ’98 and preceding the current soft-cover Philippine Style: Design and Architecture (Anvil Publishing Inc.), used that word long before it became the vogue adjective for food that takes in a variety of cultural influences. “Three hundred years in the convent, 50 in Hollywood and a brief interlude with the Japanese”–that was how eminent writer Carmen Guerrero Nakpil described the country’s colonial history and its three former masters (Spain, the US and Japan). The last didn’t quite seep in, except maybe in the sleek lines of modern architecture. Today, hard-earned dollars from overseas Filipino workers have made possible the rise of a hodge-podge of architecture flecking the countryside with houses derivative of Mediterranean villas or Mexican landlords’ haciendas and assorted misadvised kitsch coming from new money. There seems to be no acknowledgment of the wisdom inherent in the humble bahay kubo (native hut) or the gentry’s bahay na bato (house of stone), especially their factoring in of climate (harsh sun, torrential rains) and site. Architect Dominic Galicia points out in the introduction to Philippine Style that the kubo has a “geometric simplicity: a pyramidal roof hovering like a parasol over a bamboo box of stilts. Rain slid off the steeply pitched cogon roof, while fresh air, flowing in through the slatted floor and the wide windows, cooled the interior before exiting through the permeable roof thatch.” Even the Spanish-influenced bahay na bato considered the kubo an elegant and “simple solution to climate control.” Today’s discerning architect refers to these structures from the past to build buildings and houses. The book is full of examples of how parts of old houses that are increasingly being demolished to make way for townhouses and

Ladrido and BluPrint Celebrating Philippine design, 50 Years of Philippine Design and Beyond presents the evolution of Filipino design over five decades (1970-2023) at the National Museum of Fine Arts until March 3, 2024. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue. Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s. A homage to Arturo Luz, the last part of the exhibit features 50 chairs by various designers, their own interpretation of Luz’s 1982 “Buri Chair.” Curated by Marian Pastor Roces, the 200 selected objects are arranged by year, and borrowed from designers, private collectors, and the collection of the Design Center of the Philippines. Featured designers who made a significant mark in Philippine design include: Salvacion Lim Higgins (1920-1990): known as Slim’s, she modernized the look of the Philippine terno, giving it a timeless appeal and elegance. She was an educator and founder of the Slim’s Fashion and Art School, the country’s first fashion and design school which celebrated its 60 th anniversary in 2020. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022. Arturo Luz (1926-2021): A painter, printmaker, sculptor, and designer known for his abstract paintings and wood and metal sculptures, he was a founding director of the Metropolitan Museum of Manila in 1976 to 1986 and also appointed as the head of the Design Center of the Philippines. articles.text: Alex Eala/Instagram After capturing the hearts of tennis fans around the world, Alex Eala may soon start making waves in the world of fashion. The Filipina tennis star recently got the attention of no less than Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue magazine and co-chair of the Met Gala. In an interview with the US Open, Wintour observed Eala's interest in fashion based on her stylish looks on the court, and compared her to tennis greats Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka. "Well I think it's really interesting, especially when you look at players [like] Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it," she said. The fashion icon went on, referring to Eala: "And we have the young Filipino star... you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it." "And I think it's great, it's wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage." Eala was also seen in an Instagram Reel posted by Vogue. The clips were taken from an event hosted by Wintour at the Arthur Ashe Stadium, meant to celebrate Rodger Federer's return to the US Open, based on the caption. The caption referred to the guests, including Eala, as "friends of Vogue." Eala's sense of style comes as no surprise as the niece of a fashion designer. During the Laureus World Sports Awards in Madrid earlier this year, she wore a modern Filipiniana by Rhett Eala. In a previous interview with ABS-CBN News, Rhett shared that his niece reached out to him with a clear vision for her red carpet look. "Alex said that she wanted something Filipino and something in piña… She also wanted a top that she should be able to remove at the end of the night. So, she wanted to go dancing," he said. Alex Eala proudly wears Filipiniana at Laureus Awards in Madrid

It's Alex Eala 's time to serve, but this time in fashion instead of on the tennis court. On Instagram, the Filipina tennis ace got her own spotlight on the Calvin Klein account during the New York Fashion Week. Alex attended the brand's Spring 2027 runway show wearing a relaxed white long-sleeved button-down shirt paired with off-white slacks and pointed-toe heels. Following her third-round finish at this year's US Open, Alex made her New York Fashion Week debut when she attended the Tory Burch show. Earlier, Kelsey Merritt shared a photo with Alex after the two met at the Michael Kors show. Beyond tennis, Alex has also expressed her interest in fashion . During her latest visit to Manila in July, she said incorporating Filipino elements into her outfits while on tour is her way of paying tribute to her roots. Alex added that she is interested in collaborating with Filipino designers for future engagements. Meanwhile, Alex is set to headline the event " Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate " on December 8 at the Philippine Arena. She will face fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in the exhibition match. text.preview: Anna Wintour has taken notice of Alex Eala ’s interest in fashion, saying the young Filipina tennis star reflects the growing connection between sports and fashion. In a video shared by the US Open on social media, Anna discussed how athletes such as Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka have used fashion as a way to express themselves. “Well, I think it’s really interesting, especially when you look at players obviously like Serena or Naomi, who really embrace fashion and express themselves with it,” the fashion icon said. She then pointed to Alex as another young player who is showing an interest in the fashion world. “And we had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Anna said. “And I think it’s great, it’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage.” Anna gave the quick interview at sidelines of the US Open exhibition match of Roger Federer and Andy Roddick , where Alex was present with fellow tennis player Eva Lys. On Instagram Stories, Eva posted a photo with the Filipina star and wrote, "We're spectators today." Alex shared Eva's post. Vogue Magazine meanwhile shared a reel from the event that showed Anna engaging with Serena Williams and Gayle King, and Alex and Eva welcoming Vogue to the US Open. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vogue (@voguemagazine) Alex wore a cropped mustard leather top and paired it with jeans to the event. Even through fashion and accessories, Alex has proudly been representing the Philippines . Earlier this week, she donned our humble ol' tsineles that made her outfit look casually chic. Before that Alex wore pink sampaguita earrings at the Canadian Open. She also donned a sampaguita-themed hair tie in Wimbledon 2025 and a custom visor in 2026 , which had the Filipino phrase "Kapag lumago, hindi na hihinto." Alex will be competing in the US Open. MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala had a star-studded encounter off the court as she crossed paths with fashion icon Anna Wintour and Hollywood actresses Sadie Sink and Amanda Seyfried during New York Fashion Week. Eala attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 show in New York, where she was seated in the front row alongside Wintour and was in the same room with Amanda Seyfriend and musician Lauryn Hill. She also attended the Calvin Klein show with actresses Pamela Anderson, Sadie Sink, Tate McRae and Gemma Chan. The appearance marked Eala’s debut at New York Fashion Week, adding another milestone to what has been a remarkable year for the 20-year-old athlete. Eala has previously caught Wintour’s attention for her growing interest in fashion. During an interview in August, Wintour cited Eala while discussing how tennis players have increasingly used fashion to express their personalities. Wintour mentioned tennis icons Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka before turning her attention to Eala, whom she described as a young Filipino star who is already showing an interest in fashion. “You could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Wintour said. Eala admitted to Culture maganzine that she was both excited and nervous attending her first fashion week. “I’m so excited. I’m a little nervous. There’s some amazing people in this room. I’m so happy to be a part of it,” she said. She also noted the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. “Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality,” she said. The tennis star attended the Tory Burch presentation in a red blazer paired with a blue-gray striped shirt and wide brown trousers. Her New York Fashion Week appearance came after her recent campaign at the US Open, where she advanced to the third round. A post shared by Alexandra Ea

“ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour,” Keltie wrote.
Fans online were quick to react to the moment.
“Wow! Alex with Anna Wintour.. 😳😳😳 Tennis star to fashionista ❤️,” one fan wrote.

@keltieknight ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour ♬ Danceteria - Madonna Anna previously shared how Alex caught her attention, particularly because of the young athlete’s growing interest in fashion and willingness to learn more about the industry.

“We had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion. How she wants to learn about it and follow it and I think it’s great,” she said in an interview at the US Open.
“It’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage,” she added.
Aside from the Michael Kors show, Alex also attended the fashion shows of Tory Burch and Calvin Klein during the New York Fashion Week.
Tory Burch marked Alex's first event at NYFW.
In an interview with Cultured Magazine, Alex reflected on the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression.
"Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she highlighted.
At the Calvin Klein show, Alex also landed a front-row seat alongside several international stars, including Sadie Sink, Tate McRae, and Lingling Kwong.
READ: Alex Eala attends her first New York Fashion Week event Prior to attending New York Fashion Week, Alex also appeared on the US national television program CBS Mornings.

The 21-year-old tennis star also opened up about what the past year has taught her about the power of representation and how she hopes her journey can inspire others, particularly the younger generation.

"One thing I’ve learned this past year is really the power of representation and how deep of an effect inspiration can have. When I interact with the people who support me and they tell me their stories, it really touches me," she said.
"I just hope that whatever I do and the job that I have, and my day-to-day work inspires other people and inspires the youth especially to chase their dreams," she added.

MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala had a star-studded encounter off the court as she crossed paths with fashion icon Anna Wintour and Hollywood actresses Sadie Sink and Amanda Seyfried during New York Fashion Week.
Eala attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 show in New York, where she was seated in the front row alongside Wintour and was in the same room with Amanda Seyfriend and musician Lauryn Hill.
She also attended the Calvin Klein show with actresses Pamela Anderson, Sadie Sink, Tate McRae and Gemma Chan.
The appearance marked Eala’s debut at New York Fashion Week, adding another milestone to what has been a remarkable year for the 20-year-old athlete.
Eala has previously caught Wintour’s attention for her growing interest in fashion.
During an interview in August, Wintour cited Eala while discussing how tennis players have increasingly used fashion to express their personalities.
Wintour mentioned tennis icons Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka before turning her attention to Eala, whom she described as a young Filipino star who is already showing an interest in fashion.
“You could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion and how she wants to learn about it and follow it,” Wintour said.
Eala admitted to Culture maganzine that she was both excited and nervous attending her first fashion week.
“I’m so excited. I’m a little nervous. There’s some amazing people in this room. I’m so happy to be a part of it,” she said.
She also noted the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression.
“Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality,” she said.
The tennis star attended the Tory Burch presentation in a red blazer paired with a blue-gray striped shirt and wide brown trousers.
Her New York Fashion Week appearance came after her recent campaign at the US Open, where she advanced to the third round.

MANILA, Philippines — Filipina tennis star Alex Eala is continuing to take the fashion world by storm by attending more New York Fashion Week shows.
Fresh from her 3rd round exit in the US Open, Alex made her fashion week debut by attending the Spring/Summer 2027 collection launch of Tory Burch last September 10, Thursday.
The tennister was invited as an athlete guest seated front row, opting for a red blazer with black buttons, a blue-gray striped shirt underneath, and wide brown slacks.

"I'm so excited. I'm a little nervous. There's some amazing people in this room. I'm so happy to be a part of it. You know, my mom growing up really had a lot of Tory Burch shoes," Alex said at the sidelines of the red carpet.
"Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she continued.
"Sports is very physically demanding and fashion, maybe come back to me after this week and I'll know more about it."

Related: Alex Eala makes fashion week debut in New York for Tory Burch The following day Alex showed up at the Museum of Modern Art's Sculpture Garden for the Spring/Summer 2027 collection of Michael Kors, this time donning a little black dress, matching gloves, and kitten heels.
Among the attendees for that show were Lea Michele, Gabrielle Union, Olivia Munn, Kathryn Newton, Aaron Tveit, Lori Harvey, Chloe Fineman, and Natalia Bryant.
The athlete also sat front row for Calvin Klein's Spring 2027 collection by Veronica Leoni, seated in a white ensemble alongside Sadie Sink, Pamela Anderson, Gemma Chan, and Tate McRae.
Speaking to a fashion magazine, the young tennis star praised Calvin Klein's recent campaigns with Sadie and Rosalia.
"I love that in tennis we're able to express ourselves through fashion. I know that in a lot of sports maybe it's a little more restrictive," Alex said.
"You're able to show your personality in both worlds, and you know, I'm excited to explore more."
Alex will soon resume training for the Asian swing of the WTA Tour starting with the Singapore Open and the Achi-Nagoya Asian Games for Team Philippines.

— with reports from John Bryan Ulanday RELATED: Anna Wintour commends Alex Eala for fashion interest, skills Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace.

text.preview: “FUSION” seems to be the best word to describe the look of Filipino buildings and home interiors. Filipino Style , a 1997 de luxe book put out by the Department of Tourism in time for the country’s national centennial in ’98 and preceding the current soft-cover Philippine Style: Design and Architecture (Anvil Publishing Inc.), used that word long before it became the vogue adjective for food that takes in a variety of cultural influences. “Three hundred years in the convent, 50 in Hollywood and a brief interlude with the Japanese”–that was how eminent writer Carmen Guerrero Nakpil described the country’s colonial history and its three former masters (Spain, the US and Japan). The last didn’t quite seep in, except maybe in the sleek lines of modern architecture. Today, hard-earned dollars from overseas Filipino workers have made possible the rise of a hodge-podge of architecture flecking the countryside with houses derivative of Mediterranean villas or Mexican landlords’ haciendas and assorted misadvised kitsch coming from new money. There seems to be no acknowledgment of the wisdom inherent in the humble bahay kubo (native hut) or the gentry’s bahay na bato (house of stone), especially their factoring in of climate (harsh sun, torrential rains) and site. Architect Dominic Galicia points out in the introduction to Philippine Style that the kubo has a “geometric simplicity: a pyramidal roof hovering like a parasol over a bamboo box of stilts. Rain slid off the steeply pitched cogon roof, while fresh air, flowing in through the slatted floor and the wide windows, cooled the interior before exiting through the permeable roof thatch.” Even the Spanish-influenced bahay na bato considered the kubo an elegant and “simple solution to climate control.” Today’s discerning architect refers to these structures from the past to build buildings and houses. Encompassing fashion, furniture, interior, gifts and houseware, graphics, architecture, film and theater production —the exhibit provides a visual timeline of Filipino design, inspiring pride in our design heritage, material, and craftmanship. Chairs, chairs, and more chairs are everywhere, including those designed by Lor Calma, Budji Layug, Ann T. Pamintuan, and Kenneth Cobonpue. Other pieces include a purple silk taffeta pouf by Slim’s, the 2015 blue gown worn by Pia Wurzbach as the new Miss Universe, posters by Ray Albano, Narda’s ikat dyed textiles, barong tagalog, handmade paper, and book cover designs of the 1970s and 1980s. She was conferred National Artist for Fashion Design in 2022.
